newsitem.title: USA: Court delays enforcement of cable TV restrictions.
newsitem.headline: Court delays enforcement of cable TV restrictions.

text.p: Playboy Entertainment Group Inc and Graff Pay-Per-View Inc were granted a temporary reprieve from the government's plan to enforce immediately a law that tightens limits on sexually explicit programming, a spokeswoman for the U.S. Attorney's office in Delaware confirmed to Reuters.

Last week, a three judge federal panel led by Judge Jane Roth of the Third Circuit Court lifted a temporary block on enforcement of section 505 saying Playboy and Graff's constitutional challenge did not have legal merit.

Playboy and Graff moved to stop the government from enforcing section 505, which requires absolute blocking of any "bleed" from sexually explicit channels to non-subscribers, or limiting viewing to the hours of 10 pm to 6 am.
The emergency action was triggered by a Federal Communications Commission announcement on Friday that "section 505 and its associated rules are in effect."

Playboy attorney Robert Corn-Rivere told Reuters that after a telephone conference with attorneys from both sides today, "the judges agreed to issue an order delaying any enforcement until after they've had a chance to consider our motion." According to Corn-Rivere, the government's brief is due November 22 and Playboy and Graff's the Wednesday after.
